Unicode 15.0.0 collation planner fixtures

These are complete inputs captured from the unchanged Python collation verifier,
not expected values generated by the Rust planner. Each .stdin file preserves
the original UTF-8 bytes, ordering, duplicates policy and final LF. Comparison
checks the complete byte vector. It does not invoke a native collator.

Producer
  scripts/verify_collation_locales.py
  SHA256 083c685a2a15cd5db564049267eb521434eb50396adadee9c13d5899ddfdb026
Interpreter
  Python 3.12.14, built-in unicodedata, unidata_version 15.0.0
  Executable SHA256 fa67443527ed9647f760d807e2a38f26340757123e643c4639cf273ed15d5ea7
Observer
  crates/locale-tools/tests/support/collation-words-fixture.rs
  Source SHA256 f5f8e3da0176a7cfbe4f2b6c0a700db46e2de4ebee267beb109ba442e58440c9
  The safe Rust observer retained actual stdin without deriving any word plan.
Capture date
  2026-10-18

source-input-vectors.tsv is the unchanged complete 62-vector candidate index
from the two observations. SHA256 of that index is
151e2fe6cc69efa6b895196b26aa84a37cf12a786bc886af1da01c71abbdb7a4.
Both roles' bytes matched at every ordinal. All 29 block vectors also matched
between the two observations. Only these 31 distinct vectors are included:

  alphabet-mixed.stdin: mixed ordinal 00, 3458 words, 13892 bytes
  alphabet-over120.stdin: over120 ordinal 00, 266 words, 931 bytes
  named block files: mixed ordinals 02 through 30, in the index's original order

Ordinal 01 is the separate digit workload. No digit vector or duplicate block
vector is copied here. The block name order is explicit in the Rust test.

mixed.json and over120.json preserve the exact literal input configurations.
The mixed case has 36 standard-plus-ASCII strings and tests expansions, title
digraphs, full strings, combining marks, punctuation, number categories and a
standard CJK name trigger. The over120 case has 129 standard-plus-ASCII strings.
Its original 103 alphabet strings, auxiliary and tags were selected from the
retained bo_CN candidate record and placed under the fixture en_US key. The
source candidate JSON SHA256 was
d2b93c01a21a84ad5f8204155f99e7090931237d9a48127a03d229e1cb6660b0.
Neither fixture establishes native locale coverage. Fixture metadata says so.

Handwritten controls in collation_unicode.rs cover cases outside these observed
vectors. They follow these primary source contracts and are not new Python
observations:

  Unicode 15.0.0 default full case mappings and Final_Sigma context
  https://www.unicode.org/Public/15.0.0/ucd/SpecialCasing.txt

  Unicode 15.0.0 assigned CJK UNIFIED name-pattern ranges
  https://www.unicode.org/Public/15.0.0/ucd/extracted/DerivedName.txt

  Unicode 15.0.0 categories and contextual properties
  https://www.unicode.org/Public/15.0.0/ucd/extracted/DerivedGeneralCategory.txt
  https://www.unicode.org/Public/15.0.0/ucd/DerivedCoreProperties.txt

  CPython 3.12.14 original-buffer sigma and first-title/rest-lower operations
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Objects/unicodeobject.c

  CPython 3.12.14 assigned name ranges
  https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.12.14/Modules/unicodedata.c

The planner does not normalize strings, implement general Unicode names, use
language-tailored case mappings or infer a later Unicode version. The captures
establish legacy input vectors only. Native comparison, dependency qualification
and any removal of the Python collation tools are separate work.
